celaleyn:1-1.t: When it was revealed, he ﷺ said "Allahu akbar" at its end, so the takbīr at its end became a Sunna; and the command to do it at its close and at the close of every sūra after it has been narrated. It is "Allahu akbar," or "There is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest." ﴿وَالضُّحَى﴾, that is, the beginning of the day, or all of it,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَى﴾: covered with its darkness, or became still.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿مَا وَدَّعَكَ﴾: left you, O Muhammad, ﴿رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَى﴾: hated you. This was revealed when the disbelievers said, when the revelation was delayed from him for fifteen days, "His Lord has left him and hates him."

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَلَلْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَكَ﴾, because of the honours in it for you, ﴿مِنَ الْأُولَى﴾: this world.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ﴾ in the Hereafter, of good things, an abundant gift, ﴿فَتَرْضَى﴾ with it. He ﷺ said: "Then I will not be content while a single one of my community is in the Fire." Up to here the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam) is completed, with two affirmative [statements] after two negative ones.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ﴾: an interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīr), that is, He found you ﴿يَتِيمًا﴾ through the loss of your father before your birth or after it, ﴿فَآوَى﴾ by bringing you into the care of your uncle Abū Ṭālib?

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالًّا﴾ of the law that you now follow ﴿فَهَدَى﴾, that is, guided you to it,

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَوَجَدَكَ عَائِلًا﴾: poor ﴿فَأَغْنَى﴾: made you rich with what He made you content with, of war booty and other things. In the hadith: "Richness is not through an abundance of goods, but richness is richness of the soul."

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا الْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ﴾ by taking his wealth or otherwise,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا السَّائِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ﴾: rebuke him for his poverty,

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ﴾ upon you, through prophethood and other things, ﴿فَحَدِّثْ﴾: tell. His ﷺ pronoun was dropped in some of the verbs in observance of the verse-endings (fawāṣil).

daas-irab:1-2.t: ﴿وَالضُّحى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb of swearing; ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ﴾: conjoined to الضحى; ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿سَجى﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿ما﴾: negative; ﴿وَدَّعَكَ﴾: a past verb and its object; ﴿رَبُّكَ﴾: fāʿil (agent); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position; ﴿وَما قَلى﴾: conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿وَلَلْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), and الآخرة خير are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿لَكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خير; ﴿مِنَ الْأُولى﴾: attached to خير.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿وَلَسَوْفَ﴾: the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ) and سوف is a particle of the future; ﴿يُعْطِيكَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object; ﴿رَبُّكَ﴾: fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَتَرْضى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ﴾: the hamza is a particle of interrogation and affirmation (taqrīr), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿يَتِيماً﴾: second direct object; the clause is resumptive; ﴿فَآوى﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَوَجَدَكَ﴾: a past verb and its first object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿ضَالًّا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَهَدى﴾: conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition); ﴿أما﴾: a particle of condition and detailing; ﴿الْيَتِيمَ﴾: fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فَلا تَقْهَرْ﴾: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:10-10.t: Conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is clear.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿أَمَّا﴾: a particle of condition and detailing; ﴿بِنِعْمَةِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) حدث; ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿فَحَدِّثْ﴾: the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir).

farraa:1-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلضُّحَىٰ وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَىٰ﴾.
As for «الضحى», it is the whole of the daytime. ﴿وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَىٰ﴾: when it grows dark and becomes still in its length, just as you say: بحر ساج (a calm sea) and ليل ساج (a still night), when it is still, quiet and dark.

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَىٰ﴾.
It was revealed concerning the withholding of revelation from the Prophet ﷺ for fifteen [nights]. The idolaters said: Muhammad ﷺ has been forsaken by his Lord — or: the follower (al-tābiʿ) who used to be with him has come to hate him. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, revealed: ﴿مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿وَمَا قَلَىٰ﴾, meaning: وما قلاك (nor has He hated you). The kāf was dropped, just as one says: قد أعطيتك وأحسنتُ (I have given you and done well), meaning: أحسنت إليك (I have done well by you); one makes do with the first kāf rather than repeating the other. And [also] because the verse-endings are in yāʾ; so both [reasons] came together in it.

farraa:5-5.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "ولسيعطيك [ربك فترضى]", and the meaning is the same, except that (سوف) became frequent in speech and its place became well known, so the fāʾ and the wāw were left out of it; when a word becomes frequent, that is sometimes done to it, as is said: أَيشٍ تقول (what are you saying?), and as is said: قم لا بَاك and قم لا بِشانئك, meaning: لا أبا لك and لا أبا لشانئك. I have heard a verse in which the fāʾ was elided from كيف; the poet said:
من طالبين لِبُعران لنا رفضت * كيلا يُحسون من بعراننا أثرا
(From people searching for camels of ours that had strayed off — how is it that they perceive no trace of our camels?)
He meant: كيف لا يحسون (how do they not perceive?). And this is like that.

farraa:6-6.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيماً فَآوَىٰ﴾.
He says: you were in the care of Abū Ṭālib, so He gave you a shelter and made you independent of him. It was not a wealth that came from abundance of property; rather Allah made him content with what He gave him.

farraa:7-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَوَجَدَكَ ضَآلاًّ فَهَدَىٰ﴾.
He means: [He found you] among a people gone astray, and He guided you. ﴿وَوَجدَكَ عائلاً﴾ (8): poor. I saw it in the muṣḥafs of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] as "عديما" (destitute), and the meaning is the same.

farraa:8-8.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَغْنَىٰ﴾, and "فآوى": what is meant is (فأغناك) "so He enriched you" and (فآواك) "so He sheltered you". It went the way of dropping the kāf to match the verse-endings, and because the meaning is known.

farraa:9-9.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَمَّا ٱلْيَتِيمَ فَلاَ تَقْهَرْ﴾.
So that you take away his right because of his weakness. In the muṣḥaf of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is "فلا تكهر", and I heard it from a Bedouin of Banū Asad who recited it to me.

farraa:10-10.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَمَّا ٱلسَّآئِلَ فَلاَ تَنْهَرْ﴾.
The beggar at the [142/b] door. He says: either give to him, or turn him away with a gentle turning-away.

farraa:11-11.t:
His words, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ﴾.
The Qur'an was Allah's greatest blessing upon him, so he used to recite it and speak of it, and of other than it among His blessings. [Translator's note: the source reads «ويغيره», which appears to be a corruption of «وبغيره» (and of other things); translated accordingly.]

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «إذا»: a pure adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) أقسم (I swear).

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «ما ودَّعك ربك» is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam).

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The wāw is a conjunction; the lām occurs in the answer to a new oath; the preposition «لك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خير», and so is «من الأولى»; and the clause «وللآخرة خير» is conjoined to the answer to the preceding oath.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «ولسوف يعطيك ربك» is conjoined to the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), and the lām is that of the answer to an oath.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The fāʾ is resumptive; «أما»: a particle of condition and detailing; «اليتيم»: an object placed before «تقهر»; the fāʾ is the linking one; and the clause «لا تقهر» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «وأما السائل فلا تنهر» is conjoined to the clause {فَأَمَّا الْيَتِيمَ فَلا تَقْهَرْ}.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The preposition «بنعمة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «حدِّث».

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying, the Exalted: (ما ودعك): (ما) [with its clause] is the answer to the oath.
His saying (ألم يجدك يتيما): the kāf and (يتيما) are two objects of (يجد); likewise (ووجدك ضالا) and (ووجدك عائلا).
His saying (وما قلى): the object is omitted, i.e. "and He has not detested you", i.e. "and He has not hated you". (ودع) is used only with doubling; one does not say (ودع) [wadaʿa]. Sībawayh said: they dispensed with it by (ترك).

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying (فأما اليتيم فلا تقهر): (اليتيم) is accusative governed by (تقهر), and it properly belongs after the fāʾ; its implied form is "Whatever may be, do not oppress the orphan." Its like is (وأما السائل فلا تنهر). Had there been a hāʾ with (تقهر) and (تنهر), the preferred choice in (اليتيم) and (السائل) would be the nominative, with the accusative permissible; with the hāʾ omitted, only the accusative is permissible. (اليتيم) and (السائل) are nouns indicating the genus.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying (وأما بنعمة ربك فحدث): the bāʾ is attached to (حدث), and its implied place is after it; the implied form is "Whatever may be, speak of the favour of your Lord."
His saying (ولسوف يعطيك ربك): the second object is omitted, as you say "I gave you" and stop; so the implied form is "He will give you what you want, and you will be satisfied."

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿والضحى﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, and «الضحى» is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, its implied form being: "I swear" (أقسم).

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿والليل﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «الليل» is conjoined to ﴿الضحى﴾, genitive (majrūr).
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of future time, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb of oath.
﴿سجى﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "it" (هو); the clause ﴿سجى﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿ما﴾: a particle of negation.
﴿ودعك﴾: a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ربك﴾: fāʿil (agent), and the kāf is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the answer of the oath, with no grammatical position.
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿ما﴾ is a particle of negation.
﴿قلى﴾: a past verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو); the clause ﴿وما قلى﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ما ودعك﴾.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿وللآخرة﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), emphasising the content of the clause, and «الآخرة» is mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿خير﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿لك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خير﴾.
﴿من﴾: a preposition.
﴿الأولى﴾: a noun in the genitive (majrūr); the preposition and its genitive noun are also attached to ﴿خير﴾.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿ولسوف﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, the lām is of inception (ibtidāʾ), emphasising the content of the clause, and it was said: the lām is of the oath; and «سوف» is a particle of the future.
﴿يعطيك﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by a ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the kāf is a fronted object.
﴿ربك﴾: the word ﴿رب﴾ is a postponed fāʿil (agent), and the kāf is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿سوف يعطيك﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "you" (أنت), and the nominal clause is conjoined to ﴿ما ودعك﴾.
﴿فترضى﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and «ترضى» is an imperfect verb, nominative by an implied ḍamma, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت); ﴿ترضى﴾ is conjoined to ﴿يعطيك﴾.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿ألم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīrī), and «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive; the speech is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿يجدك﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو), and the kāf is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as first mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿يتيمًا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿فآوى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «آوى» is a past verb, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being: "he" (هو); ﴿آوى﴾ is conjoined to His saying ﴿ألم يجد﴾, i.e. "He found you" (وجدك). Or «وجد» means "came upon" (صادف), not in the sense of knowing; then the kāf in ﴿يجدك﴾ is mafʿūl bihi, and ﴿يتيمًا﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿ووجدك﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and «وجد» is a past verb conjoined to ﴿ألم يجد﴾, and the kāf is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ضالًّا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi, or a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿فهدى﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and «هدى» is a past verb conjoined to ﴿وجد﴾, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿ووجدك﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «وجد» is a past verb conjoined to ﴿ألم يجد﴾, and the kāf is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿عائلا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi, or a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿فأغنى﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and «أغنى» is a past verb conjoined to ﴿وجد﴾, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿فأما﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquence (al-faṣīḥa), and «أما» is a particle of condition and detailing.
﴿اليتيم﴾: a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿تقهر﴾.
﴿فلا﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and «لا» is prohibitive.
﴿تقهر﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت), i.e. "do not oppress him regarding his property".

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وأما﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and «أما» is a particle of condition and detailing.
﴿السائل﴾: a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿تنهر﴾.
﴿فلا﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and «لا» is prohibitive.
﴿تنهر﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿وأما﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and «أما» is a particle of condition and detailing.
﴿بنعمة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿حدّث﴾.
﴿ربك﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), and the kāf is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿فحدث﴾: the fāʾ links the answer of ﴿أما﴾, and «حدث» is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت); the clause ﴿فحدث﴾ is the answer of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿أما بنعمة ربك﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أما اليتيم﴾.

nahhas-irab:1-2.t:
Al-Farrāʾ said: وَالضُّحى (1) is the whole daytime. Abū Jaʿfar said: What is known among the Arabs is what Abū Rawq narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: al-ḍuḥā is the forenoon of the day.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: al-ḍuḥā is written with alif and nothing else, because it is from ḍaḥā yaḍḥū. Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of the Kufans is that it is (written) with yāʾ because its first letter has ḍamma; and this is a view that is valid neither in reason nor in analogy (qiyās), because if it is written according to the pronunciation, its pronunciation is alif, and if it is written according to the meaning (origin), it goes back to wāw.
Moreover, ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, saying: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: it is not permissible to write any of the verbs with yāʾ as third radical, such as رمى and قضى, except with alif; and the reason for that is clear from the standpoint of reason, analogy and language, because we understand that writing is only the transfer of what is in the pronunciation, just as pronunciation is the transfer of what is in the heart; so when we say رمى, there is nothing in the pronunciation but alif. If it is said: its origin is yāʾ, so he wrote it with yāʾ — it is answered: this is a mistake from more than one direction. Among them: if it were necessary to write it according to its origin, it would be necessary to write غزا with wāw, because its origin is wāw. Also, they agreed to write رماه with alif, though the alif is converted from yāʾ — and this is a contradiction. Also, there is a kind of ambiguity in this, because it could be read رُمِيَ. Then they contradicted all this and wrote verbs with wāw as third radical with yāʾ, such as ضحى and كسى, the plural of kiswa.
Abū Isḥāq said: This is the meaning of his speech — and how enormous is this mistake! — meaning their saying: words with yāʾ as third radical are written with yāʾ and those with wāw with alif; so they neither followed the pronunciation, as is required in writing, nor did they follow the codex (muṣḥaf), for in the codex ما زكى is written with yāʾ. Abū Isḥāq said:
Greater than their mistake in writing is their mistake in the dual, because they make the dual of ربا ribayān, and this is contrary to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; He said: وَما آتَيْتُمْ مِنْ رِباً لِيَرْبُوَا فِي أَمْوالِ النَّاسِ فَلا يَرْبُوا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ [al-Rūm: 39], i.e., the Qur'an came with wāw, and they came with yāʾ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I said to Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, when he had argued with these irrefutable arguments: "What is this that has befallen the scribes, to which the elite and the common people have grown accustomed, of writing words with yāʾ as third radical with yāʾ, so that it has become the accepted convention?" He said: The origin of this is that Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash was a man who used stratagems for something to take (i.e., to earn), so he said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Kisāʾī: "Those whom we need have become independent of grammar, so we need to agree on something by which we compel them (to need us)". So the two agreed on this and introduced it; it did not exist before them, and it spread among people because of al-Kisāʾī's standing with the ruler. Perhaps someone who does not investigate thoroughly imagines that this is the doctrine of Sībawayh, because something in his words on the like of it was unclear to him — his saying "the yāʾ in the like of سكرى" — whereas Sībawayh only meant that it takes yāʾ in the dual; and giving reasons for orthography is not part of Sībawayh's discussion.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Then we return to the imāla (inclination of the vowel ā toward ē). Ḥamza applies imāla to what has yāʾ as third radical and pronounces with tafkhīm (full ā) what has wāw as third radical; al-Kisāʾī applies imāla to all of it; Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ makes some of the words follow others, so if the sūra has both words with yāʾ and words with wāw he applies imāla to all; and the Medinans take a middle course, neither inclining fully nor giving full tafkhīm. Abū Jaʿfar said: There is no mistake in any of these approaches, because imāla is permissible in verbs with wāw as third radical, since they go back to yāʾ. So «والضحى» and وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا سَجى (2) are permissible with imāla, even though one says سجا يسجو, because it goes back to yāʾ in your saying سجيت.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: It has been said: i.e., convey (it), i.e., make it manifest and praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for it, for that is part of gratitude.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: (وَما قَلى means) "nor has He hated you". Abū Jaʿfar said: The Arabs omit from the second (verb) because the first indicates it; one says: أعطيتك وأكرمت ("I gave you and honoured", i.e., honoured you). Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ما ودّعك ربّك وما قلى, he said: He says: He has not abandoned you and has not hated you. Abū ʿUbayda reported ودَعك without doubling; and Sībawayh disallowed saying ودع (in the past), saying: they made do without it by using ترك. Abū Jaʿfar said: The reason according to others is that the Arabs find wāw heavy at the start of a word because of its heaviness. What indicates this is that it is not found as an augment at the start of a word, while its sister the yāʾ is found, as in yaʿmala and yarbūʿ; and that when you form the diminutive of wāṣil you say uwayṣil and nothing else, and in the plural awāṣil. One says: qalāhu yaqlīhi when he hates him, and one also says yaqlāhu.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: The original (of خير) is أخير; then it was lightened because of frequent use.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضى (5): in the version (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd) «وسيعطيك», and the two are one (in meaning) according to Sībawayh. Al-Farrāʾ said:
The wāw and the fāʾ (of سوف) were dropped, just as they said أيش عندها ("what does she have?") and as they said لاب لشانئك and لاب لك, meaning لا أب لشانئك and لا أب لك ("your hater has no father", "you have no father"). Abū Jaʿfar said: The second object was omitted, just as you say "I gave Zayd" without specifying the gift.

nahhas-irab:6-7.t: أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيماً فَآوى (6): (يتيما is) an object of يجد. And يجد in the speech of the Arabs divides into several kinds, among them that it is in the sense of يرى and تعلم (to see, to know), and likewise وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالًّا فَهَدى (7).

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: ʿĀla yaʿīlu ʿaylatan, when he becomes poor; and aʿāla yuʿīlu, when his dependants become many. We know of no disagreement among the scholars of the language about this.

nahhas-irab:9-10.t: فَأَمَّا الْيَتِيمَ is accusative by تقهر; and even if it were تقهره with the hāʾ, the accusative would still be preferred, because it is a prohibition. And likewise وَأَمَّا السَّائِلَ فَلا تَنْهَرْ (10).

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {سجى}: It was said: its meaning is "grew still." From it: «سجا البحر يَسْجُو سَجْواً», i.e. its waves became still; and «طَرْفٌ ساجٍ», i.e. a languid eye. From it, «تَسْجِيَةُ الميتِ», i.e. covering him with a cloth, is borrowed figuratively. Al-Rāghib said this. Al-Aʿshā said:

4589 - وما ذَنْبُنا إنْ جاش بَحْرُ ابنِ عَمِّكُمْ ... وبَحْرُكَ ساجٍ لا يُوارِي الدَّعامِصا
(What is our fault if your cousin's sea surges, while your sea is still, not hiding even the small fish?)

It was said: «سجا» means "went away"; and the opposite was also said. Al-Farrāʾ said: "grew dark." Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: "its darkness became intense." The poet said:

4590 - يا حَبَّذا القَمْراءُ والليلُ السَّاجْ ... وطُرُقٌ مِثْلُ مُلاءِ النِّسَّاجْ
(How lovely is the moonlit night, the still night, and paths like the weaver's sheet!)

It is of the class of words with wāw as the third radical; it is pronounced with imāla (leaning of the vowel) only to agree with the verse-endings, like «الضُّحى», which is also of the class with wāw.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {مَا وَدَّعَكَ}: This is the apodosis (jawāb) [of the oath]. The majority read it with doubling of the dāl, from التَوْديع (bidding farewell). ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, his son Hishām, Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it without doubling, from their saying: وَدَعَه, i.e. he left him. What is well known in the language is that وَدَعَ and وَذَرَ, their active participle, their passive participle and their verbal noun are dispensed with in favour of «تَرَكَ» and its derived forms; yet وَدَعَ and وَذَرَ have occurred. The poet said:
4591 - سَلْ أميري ما الذي غَيَّرَهْ ... عن وِصالي اليومَ حتى وَدَعَهْ
(Ask my lord what changed him from his union with me today, so that he abandoned it.)
And the poet said:
4592 - وثُمَّ وَدَعْنا آلَ عمروٍ وعامرٍ ... فرائِسَ أَطْرافِ المُثَقَّفةِ السُّمْرِ
(And there we left the families of ʿAmr and ʿĀmir as prey to the tips of the straightened brown spears.)
It was said: التوديع is an intensification of الوَدْع, because whoever bids you farewell on parting has gone to the extreme in leaving you.
His saying: {وَمَا قلى}, i.e. He did not hate you. قلاه يَقْليه, with kasra on the middle radical in the imperfect; and [the tribe of] Ṭayyiʾ say: قلاه يقلاه with fatḥa. The poet said:
4593 - أيا مَنْ لَسْتُ أَنْساه ... ولا واللَّهِ أَقْلاه
لكَ اللَّهُ على ذاكَ ... لكَ اللَّهُ [لكَ اللَّهُ]
(O you whom I do not forget, and — no, by Allah — whom I do not hate: Allah is your witness to that, Allah is your witness, [Allah is your witness].)
The object of «قَلَى» was omitted out of regard for the verse-endings (fawāṣil), since it is known; likewise after «فآوى» and what follows it.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {وَلَلآخِرَةُ}: What is apparent regarding this lām is that it is [the lām of] the apodosis (jawāb) of the oath, and likewise in «ولَسَوْفَ». He the Exalted swore upon four things: two negated, namely His bidding him farewell and His hating him; and two affirmed and emphasised, namely the Hereafter being better for him than this world, and that He will give him what will make him content. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: what is this lām that enters upon "سَوْف"? I say: it is the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ) that emphasises the content of the clause, and the mubtadaʾ (subject) is omitted, its implied form being: "ولأنت سَوْفَ يُعْطيك" (and you — He will give you), as we mentioned at {لاَ أُقْسِمُ} [al-Qiyāma: 1] that the meaning is: "لأَنا أُقْسِمُ" (I indeed swear). That is because it must be either the lām of the oath or [the lām] of commencement. The lām of the oath does not enter the imperfect except together with the nūn of emphasis; so it remains that it is the lām of commencement, and the lām of commencement enters only upon a clause made of a mubtadaʾ and a khabar (predicate); so a [mubtadaʾ] and its khabar must be supplied, and its origin is: ولأنت سوف يعطيك.» The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] transmitted from him that he said: «And its indication of the present was stripped from the lām.» End of quotation. Of these [two alternatives] that al-Zamakhsharī turned over, the one to be chosen is that it is the lām of the oath.
His saying: «It does not enter the imperfect except with the nūn of emphasis» — the grammarians excepted two cases from this. The first: that no particle of futurity (ḥarf tanfīs) be placed between it and the verb, as in this verse, as in your saying: واللَّهِ لَسَأُعْطيك (by Allah, I will surely give you). The second: that no governed word of the verb be placed between them, as in His saying, the Exalted: {لإِلَى الله تُحْشَرُونَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 158]. [Translator's note: in both cases the text reads «أن لا يُفْصَل» ("that … not be placed between"), yet both the verse and the examples show the lām separated from the verb (by سوف/السين and by إلى الله respectively); the intended sense is evidently "that … be placed between".] What I have said is supported by what al-Fārisī said: «This lām is not the one in your saying: "إنَّ زيداً لَقائمٌ"; rather, it is the one in your saying: "لأَقومَنَّ" (I will surely stand), and "سوفَ" has substituted for one of the two nūns of emphasis, so it is as if He said: ولَيُعْطِيَنَّك (and He will surely give you).»
And his saying: «its indication of the present was stripped from it» means that the lām of commencement, when it enters the imperfect, restricts it to the present; here that is not possible because of the particle of futurity, so the present sense was stripped from it.
The Shaykh said: «The lām in "ولَلآخرةُ" is a lām of commencement that emphasised the content of the clause.» Then he related some of what I have mentioned from al-Zamakhsharī and Abū ʿAlī [al-Fārisī], then said: «In my view it is possible that the lām in "وللآخرةُ خيرٌ" and in "ولَسَوْفَ يُعْطيك" is the lām by which the oath is answered, He having conjoined it onto the apodosis of the oath, namely His saying: {مَا وَدَّعَكَ}; so He would have sworn upon these three.» End of quotation. Its apparent sense is that the lām in «ولَلآخرةُ» is a lām of commencement not answering the oath, as shown by his saying secondly: «In my view it is possible». But the disconnection of this clause from the apodosis of the oath is not apparent at all, and likewise in {ولَسَوْفَ}; and al-Zamakhsharī's supplying a mubtadaʾ after it does not contradict its being an apodosis of the oath; he only prevented its being an apodosis [lām] entering upon the imperfect in wording and in implied form.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {فآوى}: The majority read «آوى» with an alif after the hamza, as a quadriliteral, from آواه يُؤْوِيْهِ (he gave him shelter). Abū al-Ashhab [read] «فأوى» as a triliteral. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It has two meanings: either from "أواه" in the sense of "آواه" — one of the herdsmen was heard saying: "أين آوي هذه" (where shall I shelter these?) — or from أوى له, when he took pity on him.» End of quotation. On the second [meaning] is his saying:
4594 - أراني - ولا كفرانَ لله - أيَّةُ ... لنفسي لقد طالَبْتُ غيرَ مُنيلِ
(I see myself — and no ingratitude to Allah — out of pity for myself: I have indeed made demands of one who does not give.)
i.e. out of pity for myself. The point of evidence in his saying: «saying: أين آوي هذه» is that had it been from the quadriliteral he would have said «أُؤْوي» with ḍamma on the first hamza and sukūn on the second, because it is the imperfect of «آوى» like أَكْرَمَ; this ḍamma-voweled hamza is the imperfect prefix, and the second is the first radical of the word, while the hamza of أَفْعَل is omitted according to the rule. This hamza was not replaced, as it was replaced in «أُوْمِنُ أنا», lest it become heavy through assimilation; that is why the Qurʾān readers stipulated that «تُؤْويه» in His saying «وفَصيلتِه التي تُؤْويه» may not be replaced, because of the heaviness.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {عَآئِلاً}, i.e. poor. This is the reading of the majority. One says: عال زيدٌ, i.e. he became poor. Jarīr said:
4595 - اللهُ نَزَّل في الكتابِ فريضةً ... لابنِ السبيل وللفقيرِ العائلِ
(Allah sent down in the Book an obligatory share for the wayfarer and for the needy poor.)
And أعال: his dependants became many. He said:
4596 - ومايَدْري الفقيرُ متى غِناه ... وما يَدْري الغَنِيُّ متى يُعيلُ
(The poor man does not know when he will become rich, nor does the rich man know when he will become poor.)
Al-Yamānī read «عَيِّلاً» with kasra on the doubled yāʾ, like سَيِّد.

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {فَأَمَّا اليتيم}: accusative by «تَقْهَرْ». Shaykh Ibn Mālik — may Allah have mercy on him — took it as evidence that the placing first of the governed word does not entail [the permissibility of] placing first the governor. Do you not see that «اليتيمَ» is made accusative by the jussive verb and has been placed before the jussive-making particle, whereas if you placed «تَقْهَرْ» before «لا» it would be prohibited, because a jussive verb does not precede what makes it jussive, just as a genitive does not precede what makes it genitive? This has been discussed in Sūrat Hūd at His saying, the Exalted: {أَلاَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمْ لَيْسَ مَصْرُوفاً عَنْهُمْ} [Hūd: 8]. The majority read «تَقْهَرْ» with qāf, from overpowering. Ibn Masʿūd, al-Shaʿbī and Ibrāhīm al-Taymī [read it] with kāf. One says: كَهَرَ في وجهه, i.e. he frowned; and فلان ذو كُهْرُوْرة, i.e. frowning of face; and from it is the ḥadīth: «فبأبي وأمي هو ما كَهَرني» (may my father and mother be his ransom, he did not frown at me). Al-Zamakhsharī said this. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: «It is a dialectal form with the meaning of the reading of the majority.» End of quotation. الكَهْر originally is the rising of the day with intense heat.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «حَدِّثْ», and the fāʾ does not prevent that. This has already been discussed.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَى (٣)).
The words of the Exalted (وَدَّعَكَ): with a doubled consonant (tashdīd); it has also been read with a single one (takhfīf), which is a rare dialectal form. Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī said:
لَيْتَ شِعْرِي عَنْ خَلِيلِي مَا الَّذِي غَالَهُ فِي الْحُبِّ حَتَّى وَدَعَهُ
(Would that I knew, about my friend, what befell him in love until he abandoned it), that is, he left love.
The words of the Exalted (وَمَا قَلَى): the alif is substituted for a yāʾ, because they say «قَلَيْتُهُ» (I hated him); the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted, i.e. «وَمَا قَلَاكَ» (nor has He hated you). Likewise: «فَآوَاكَ», «فَهَدَاكَ» and «فَأَغْنَاكَ». [Translator's note: the author cites these with the object pronoun as it is understood; in the muṣḥaf the verbs read «فَآوَى», «فَهَدَى», «فَأَغْنَى», with the object omitted.]

ukberi-tibyan:9-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَمَّا الْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ (٩) وَأَمَّا السَّائِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ (١٠) وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ (١١)).
(الْيَتِيمَ) is accusative (manṣūb) by what comes after it, and likewise «السَّائِلَ».
(بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «حَدِّثْ», and the fāʾ does not prevent that, because it is like a redundant (zāʾida) particle.

zajjaj:1-2.t:
Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿والضُّحى﴾ ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذا سَجى﴾: this is an oath, and its answer is ﴿ما ودَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وما قَلى﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā: 3]. ”اَلضُّحى“ is the daytime; and it was said: one of the hours of the day. And His saying ”إذا سَجى“ means "when it is still". The poet said:
يا حَبَّذا القَمْراءُ واللَّيْلُ السّاجْ ∗∗∗ وطُرُقٌ مِثْلُ مُلاءِ النَّسّاجْ
(How lovely the moonlit night and the still [al-sāj] night, and roads like the sheets of the weaver!)

zajjaj:3-3.t: And the meaning of ﴿ما ودَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وما قَلى﴾ is: He has not cut off revelation from you, nor has He hated you. That is because revelation was delayed from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for fifteen days, and some people said: "Muhammad's companion has bidden him farewell and hated him." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down: ﴿ما ودَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وما قَلى﴾. The meaning is "nor has He hated you", as He said: ﴿والذّاكِرِينَ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا والذّاكِراتِ﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 35] ("and the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember"), the meaning being "and the women who remember Him".

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying: ﴿ألَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَآوى﴾ ("did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter?"): the Prophet, peace be upon him, was in the care of his uncle Abū Ṭālib.

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying: ﴿وَوَجَدَكَ ضالا فَهَدى﴾ ("and He found you wandering and guided you"): its meaning — and Allah knows best — is that he did not know the Qur'an or the revealed laws, so Allah guided him to the Qur'an and the laws of Islam. The evidence for that is His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ رُوحًا مِن أمْرِنا ما كُنْتَ تَدْرِي ما الكِتابُ ولا الإيمانُ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 52] ("and thus We revealed to you a spirit of Our command; you did not know what the Book was, nor faith"). And some people said: he was upon the way of his people for forty years.

zajjaj:9-9.t: And His saying: ﴿فَأمّا اليَتِيمَ فَلا تَقْهَرْ﴾ ("so as for the orphan, do not oppress"): that is, do not overpower him regarding his property.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَأمّا السّائِلَ فَلا تَنْهَرْ﴾ ("and as for the one who asks, do not repel"): that is, do not rebuff him; either give to him, or turn him away with a gentle turning away.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿وَأمّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ﴾ ("and as for the favour of your Lord, proclaim it"): that is, convey what you have been sent with, and speak of the prophethood which Allah has given you, which is the greatest of favours.
